quizzes.title: PIO and OCI Schemes: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage:
Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) are two schemes that link people of Indian heritage living abroad with India. The OCI scheme was introduced through an amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955. The PIO and OCI schemes were later merged into a single arrangement. The booklet presents the two categories side by side under the heading PIO VS OCI.

A foreign citizen can qualify as a PIO if a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent was born in India and was a permanent resident of India. The definition also covers a foreign citizen who is the spouse of a citizen of India or of a PIO, and it carves out exceptions for nationals of certain countries. PIO card holders enjoy parity with NRIs in economic, financial and educational benefits, and any future benefits given to NRIs are also available to PIO card holders.

OCI registration is open to certain foreign nationals with links to India, and minor children of such persons are also eligible. Registered OCI holders receive a multipurpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa. This visa allows the holder to visit India at any time, for any length of time and for any purpose.

The booklet sets out who qualifies for each category and what benefits each one provides, with separate sections for each.

questions.q: Nationals of which of the following countries are excluded from the definition of a Person of Indian Origin (PIO)?
questions.explanation: The booklet excludes nationals of Pakistan, among other countries, from the PIO definition.

questions.q: For how many years from the date of issue does a PIO card holder need no visa to visit India?
questions.explanation: PIO card holders need no visa for 15 years from the date of issue of the card.

questions.q: Which right is excluded from the parity that OCI holders enjoy with NRIs in economic, financial and education fields?
questions.explanation: OCI holders have parity with NRIs in these fields except the right to acquire agricultural or plantation properties.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A PIO card holder whose stay in India is up to 180 days is exempt from registration at FRRO/FRO.
Reason (R): OCI holders are exempt from police reporting for any length of stay in India.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason concerns OCI holders and does not explain the PIO registration exemption.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Reference date for persons eligible to become an Indian citizen (OCI)   ->   A. 26.01.1950
II. Days to register with FRRO/FRO after a stay exceeds 180 days (PIO)   ->   B. 30 days
III. Date after which a territory became part of India (OCI)   ->   C. 15.08.1947
IV. Scheme whose holders are exempt from police reporting   ->   D. OCI
questions.explanation: I matches A, II matches B, III matches C and IV matches D.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about PIO and OCI:
I. A person who was ever a citizen of Bangladesh is not eligible for OCI registration.
II. PIO card holders need no visa to visit India for 15 years from the date of issue of the card.
III. OCI holders have the right to acquire agricultural or plantation properties.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III contradicts the OCI property exception.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Nationals of Nepal are excluded from the definition of a PIO.
A PIO card holder staying in India for 200 days must register with FRRO/FRO within 30 days.
OCI holders must report to the police for any stay longer than 180 days.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The first two statements match the booklet, while the third contradicts the OCI exemption from police reporting.

quizzes.title: PIO and OCI Schemes: Typed Answer Practice
quizzes.passage:
The booklet compares two schemes for people of Indian heritage living abroad: the Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) scheme and the Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) scheme. The OCI scheme began as an amendment to the Citizenship Act, and the two schemes were later merged into one arrangement.

A foreign citizen qualifies as a PIO when a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent was born in India and was a permanent resident of India. The definition also covers a foreign citizen who is the spouse of a citizen of India or of a PIO, and it excludes nationals of certain countries. PIO card holders have parity with NRIs in economic, financial and educational benefits.

OCI registration is open to certain foreign nationals with links to India. Minor children of an eligible person are also eligible. OCI holders are exempt from police reporting for any length of stay in the country. They enjoy parity with NRIs in the economic, financial and education fields, but they have no right to acquire agricultural or plantation properties.

The booklet describes both categories with their eligibility and benefits. It presents these rules for each scheme separately, under the heading PIO VS OCI, and lists the benefits of each category in turn.

questions.q: For how many years from the date of issue does a PIO card holder need no visa to visit India? (answer in years)
questions.explanation: PIO card holders need no visa for 15 years from the date of issue of the card.

questions.q: Up to what length of stay, in days, is a PIO exempt from registration at FRRO/FRO?
questions.explanation: A PIO whose stay does not exceed 180 days is exempted from FRRO/FRO registration.

questions.q: If a PIO's stay goes beyond that limit, within how many days must the PIO register with FRRO/FRO? (answer in days)
questions.explanation: Such a PIO must register with FRRO/FRO within the next 30 days.

questions.q: Persons who were eligible to become citizens of India on which date (DD.MM.YYYY) qualify for OCI registration?
questions.explanation: The OCI eligibility rule refers to persons eligible to become citizens of India on 26.01.1950.

questions.q: Persons from a territory that became part of India after which date (DD.MM.YYYY) are eligible for OCI registration?
questions.explanation: OCI eligibility extends to those who belonged to a territory that became part of India after 15.08.1947.

questions.q: Apart from Pakistan, a person who was ever a citizen of which country is ineligible for OCI registration?
questions.explanation: A person who had ever been a citizen of Bangladesh, like Pakistan, is not eligible for OCI.

questions.q: Besides 'multipurpose' and 'lifelong', what single word describes the entry type of the OCI visa?
questions.explanation: The OCI visa is described as multipurpose, multiple-entry and lifelong.

quizzes.title: Sri Lanka Profile: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage:
The booklet covers Sri Lanka's capital, leaders and ties with India, and its profile of the country names the Palk Strait as the border between the two countries. Colombo is the executive capital of Sri Lanka, and Harini Amarasuriya serves as its Prime Minister. The Vice President made his first-ever bilateral visit to Sri Lanka and held talks in Colombo. The booklet records this visit under the heading Why in News.

The booklet describes India's cooperation with Sri Lanka in several areas, including development projects and maritime rescue. India and Sri Lanka jointly commission a Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka also takes part in multilateral cooperation, which includes BIMSTEC, SAARC and the Colombo Security Conclave.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) was formed as a self-styled 'National Freedom Movement of People of Tamil Eelam'. The group undertook terrorist activities in Sri Lanka. The booklet also links the LTTE to the assassination of Rajiv Gandhi, a former Prime Minister of India.

Chinese vessels named Shi Yan-6 and Yuan Wang-5 conduct data collection, which the booklet describes as potentially supporting military operations against India. This topic appears in the April 2026 issue of the booklet, under the International Relations and News chapter.

questions.q: In which year was the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) formed?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the LTTE was formed in 1976.

questions.q: Who is the President of Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Anura Kumara Dissanayake as President, while Harini Amarasuriya is the Prime Minister.

questions.q: What is the currency of Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the Sri Lankan Rupee as the currency of Sri Lanka.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 13th Amendment of the Sri Lankan Constitution led to Provincial Councils with power-sharing for all 9 provinces.
Reason (R): China's growing influence in Sri Lanka runs through financial aid and Hambantota Port.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the Chinese influence point does not explain the provincial arrangements created by the Amendment.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Joint naval exercise between India and Sri Lanka   ->   A. SLINEX
II. Joint army exercise between India and Sri Lanka   ->   B. MITRA SHAKTI
III. Multi-lateral naval exercise   ->   C. MILAN
IV. Regional forum of the Indian Ocean rim   ->   D. Indian Ocean Rim Association
questions.explanation: SLINEX is the naval exercise, MITRA SHAKTI the army exercise, MILAN the multi-lateral naval exercise and the Indian Ocean Rim Association the regional forum.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India supports the development of Trincomalee as a Regional Energy and Industrial Hub.
II. The Sampur Solar Power Plant is being constructed in Sri Lanka.
III. The LTTE undertook terrorist activities mainly against Tamils.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III contradicts its statement that the LTTE's terrorist activities were especially against Sinhalese.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Sri Lanka joins the International Big Cat Alliance.
II. SLINEX is an army exercise conducted between India and Sri Lanka.
III. The India-Sri Lanka Free Trade Agreement was signed in 2000.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is wrong because SLINEX is a naval exercise.

quizzes.title: Sri Lanka Profile: Typed Answer Practice
quizzes.passage:
The booklet covers Sri Lanka's leadership, currency and international relations. The country's President is Anura Kumara Dissanayake, and its currency is the Sri Lankan Rupee. The profile also names the Palk Strait as the border between India and Sri Lanka.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam was formed in 1976 as a self-styled 'National Freedom Movement of People of Tamil Eelam'. The group undertook terrorist activities in Sri Lanka. The booklet also links the LTTE to the assassination of Rajiv Gandhi, a former Prime Minister of India.

India and Sri Lanka jointly commission a Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Sri Lanka. The booklet lists the Sampur Solar Power Plant under development cooperation, and it lists the naval exercises SLINEX and MILAN among joint exercises between the two countries. The booklet also records the completion of Phase III of the Indian Housing Project, and it lists Memoranda of Understanding signed under a Multi-Sectoral Grant Assistance Programme, with healthcare and women's empowerment as focus areas.

Sri Lanka's multilateral cooperation includes BIMSTEC, SAARC and the Indian Ocean Rim Association. The India-Sri Lanka Free Trade Agreement was signed in 2000, and Sri Lanka joined the International Big Cat Alliance during the Vice President's visit. This topic appears in the April 2026 issue of the booklet.

questions.q: Who is the Prime Minister of Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Harini Amarasuriya as Sri Lanka's Prime Minister.

questions.q: Which city is the executive capital of Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Colombo as the executive capital, while Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte houses the legislature.

questions.q: Which numbered amendment to the Sri Lankan Constitution led to the creation of Provincial Councils? (give the number only)
questions.explanation: The 13th Amendment led to Provincial Councils with power-sharing for all 9 provinces.

questions.q: How many Chinese vessels are named in the booklet as conducting data collection? (answer as a number)
questions.explanation: The booklet names two Chinese vessels, Shi Yan-6 and Yuan Wang-5, as conducting data collection.

questions.q: Which Sri Lankan city is being developed as a Regional Energy and Industrial Hub with Indian support?
questions.explanation: India supports the development of Trincomalee as a Regional Energy and Industrial Hub.

questions.q: Which port in Sri Lanka is part of China's growing influence through financial aid?
questions.explanation: China's growing influence in Sri Lanka runs through financial aid and Hambantota Port.

questions.q: Which branch of the armed forces takes part in the India-Sri Lanka exercise MITRA SHAKTI?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists MITRA SHAKTI as the joint exercise of the Army.
